content: The Roundabout PlayPump is an innovative water pump system that harnesses the kinetic energy generated by children playing on a merry-go-round to pump water from underground sources. This system is manufactured by the South African company Roundabout Outdoor and operates similarly to a windmill-driven water pump. It is designed to be cost-effective, with an approximate price of R96,000 (around USD $14,000), making it suitable for shared use in villages, particularly in areas where water must be accessed from deep underground boreholes, reaching depths of up to 100 meters. Currently, there are over 700 PlayPumps installed across sub-Saharan Africa, providing clean drinking water to more than one million impoverished individuals. A public-private partnership has committed $4 million to expand the installation of PlayPumps, with the goal of deploying 4,000 pumps to supply water to up to 10 million people in Africa by 2010. This initiative has received significant funding, including $4 million from The MCJ Foundation. The PlayPump water system is designed as a playground merry-go-round connected to a water pump. As children spin the merry-go-round, underground water is pumped into a 2,500-liter storage tank elevated seven meters above the ground. The water stored in the tank can be easily accessed through a tap valve. According to the manufacturer, the pump is capable of raising up to 1,400 liters of water per hour from a depth of 40 meters. Any excess water is redirected back underground. The storage tank features a four-sided advertising panel, with two sides used for commercial advertisements to fund pump maintenance and the other two sides dedicated to public health messages, such as HIV/AIDS prevention. There are now more than 900 PlayPumps installed in four countries within sub-Saharan Africa, providing clean drinking water to approximately one million people in need. The sub-Saharan region faces a severe lack of access to clean water, coupled with the highest prevalence of HIV/AIDS in the world. The PlayPump not only delivers clean water but also disseminates potentially life-saving public health messages to help curb the spread of the virus. This dual-purpose system earned the World Bank’s Development Marketplace Award in 2000 for its effectiveness in both water pumping and health communication. Beyond the health benefits of clean, accessible drinking water, the PlayPump offers recreational opportunities for children and alleviates the burden of water collection. Children can spend more time in school instead of fetching water, and women, who previously had to transport heavy water containers over long distances, can dedicate more time to household responsibilities or engage in activities that generate additional food or income for their families. Roundabout Outdoor is the company responsible for manufacturing, installing, and maintaining PlayPump water systems throughout sub-Saharan Africa. PlayPumps International, a nonprofit organization, raises funds to donate these systems to African communities and schools. It is registered as a U.S. 501(c)(3) organization and as an independent South African non-governmental organization. Roundabout Outdoor collaborates with PlayPumps International to provide these systems to communities in need of clean drinking water. PlayPumps have also been installed in attractions around the world to raise awareness about how these simple yet transformative systems benefit African communities. Related topics include initiatives like the Blood:Water Mission and discussions on water privatization in South Africa.
